name: pty
description: Owns a persistent terminal process, screen/output events, shell commands, and environment discovery.

pty.description: The shared terminal: {op, ...} for read, commands, screen, viewport, frame, scroll, write, resize, print, key, mouse, paste, focus, control and context_metadata.

environment.description: The boot-time scan of the host (shell, OS, user, cwd, PATH, executables) plus the current shell identity; takes no arguments.

tool.shell.description: The shell tool: {op: describe} for its description, {op: call, input, context} to run a command line, send input or read the screen, {op: cancel, context} to interrupt a matching invocation.

command.description: One command line, submitted at the shell prompt.

input.description: Literal terminal input, sent exactly as supplied to the foreground program.

timeout_ms.description: Readback wait; default 1000 for commands, 200 for input, 0 for reads. Does not kill the program.

context.description: The invocation: session, run, call and cwd of the caller.

pty.output.description: Terminal output as it arrives: {n, data} (base64 chunk), {command} (a finished command), {exit} (shell exit) or {control, interrupted} (a handoff).

shell.doc: The shell a hosted terminal runs. Absent takes `$SHELL`, then `/bin/sh`.

scrollback.doc: Rows a terminal keeps for scrolling back.

limits.context_bytes.doc: Bytes of terminal context rendered for a caller.

limits.text_bytes.doc: Bytes of one identity text field.

limits.identity_bytes.doc: Bytes of the whole identity record.

limits.grid_margin.doc: Rows of headroom the grid keeps above the scrollback depth, so its own ring never trims first.

limits.ring_bytes.doc: Bytes of output the ring keeps.

limits.scrollback.doc: Default scrollback when `scrollback` above names none.

limits.output_bytes.doc: Bytes of one command's output kept against its mark.

limits.whole_read_lines.doc: Lines a file may have before `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `less` or `more` of it alone, with no pipe or redirection, is refused and pointed at tool.digest.

limits.carry_bytes.doc: Bytes carried forward from the previous command.
